title: Active Graph Agent Runtime (BabyAGI 4) — Yohei Nakajima, Untapped Capital
talk_summary: Yohei Nakajima presents Active Graph, an event-sourced runtime where an immutable typed event log is the source of truth and 'behaviors' react to graph changes instead of LLMs calling each other directly.

takeaways.technique: Event-sourced log as shared state instead of agent-to-agent messaging
takeaways.what_they_do: All agents/behaviors communicate only through an immutable typed event log that projects a queryable graph; behaviors subscribe to graph changes and emit events, so no direct LLM-to-LLM calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: LLMs don't talk to each other in ActiveGraph. They all communicate through this shared state

takeaways.what_they_do: Because state is derived from an append-only log, a crashed run resumes from the last event instead of restarting; the speaker's eval run resumed at question 353 after an API key failure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it just like rolled back one and was like, "All right, we'll just start from, you know, question number 353."
takeaways.numbers: resumed at question 353 of 500 instead of restarting

takeaways.technique: Graph-query views as programmatic context management
takeaways.what_they_do: Each behavior gets a scoped subset of the graph (a 'view') as its context, defined as a graph query, rather than dumping full history.
takeaways.evidence_quote: context management can be done programmatically as basically a graph query... grab a subset of the graph, which makes it available to that behavior

takeaways.what_they_do: Policies define which changes an agent may make autonomously vs. which require a proposed patch, tests, or human approval (e.g., editing prompts or facts needs gating).
takeaways.evidence_quote: some graph changes require a proposed patch before approval... what it's allowed to change by itself

takeaways.technique: Self-modification loop with static + sandbox + measured-outcome gates
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent proposes a change to itself, runs a static gate check, a sandbox gate check, then measures whether accuracy actually improved on a held-out question set; only accepted if it did, and rejected attempts are recorded.
takeaways.evidence_quote: doing a static gate check, a sandbox gate check, and then making sure it actually impacted the result, and only then accepted a change
takeaways.numbers: looped 8-13 times, accepted only 4-5 patches; modest but statistically significant improvement on LongMemEval

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of pure vector RAG, embed the query, find relevant messages in the structured log, and pull a few messages before/after to preserve ordering, fitting to context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I just embedded the query, looked for relevant messages, grabbed a couple messages before and after, made sure it fit into the context
takeaways.numbers: did 'pretty well' on LongMemEval with no semantic/fact/entity extraction
